chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best way to make up the optional prayers is to make up the night prayers at night, and the day prayers during the day.' I said, 'So there will be two Witr prayers in one night?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said, 'And why do you order me to pray Witr and two Witr prayers in one night?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'One of them is a make-up (qada)'.

key_terms.قَضَاء: Make-up prayer (performing a missed obligatory or optional prayer after its time has passed)
key_terms.وِتْر: Witr (an odd-numbered prayer, often performed at night)

ai.seo_question: How should one make up missed optional night prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of temporal fidelity in making up missed voluntary prayers, emphasizing that night prayers should be compensated at night and day prayers during the day to preserve their specific spiritual character. This guidance clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of performing two Witr prayers in a single night, where one serves as the make-up (qada) for the missed night prayer while the other remains a fresh voluntary act, thereby maintaining the integrity of both the obligation and the supererogatory nature of the worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Al-Ju’fy who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘The best way of fulfilling the optional (Salāts) is fulfilling the (outstanding) night ones at night, and the (outstanding) day ones at daytime’. I said, ‘So, can there be two Al-Witr (Salāts) at night?’ Heasws said: ‘No’. I said, ‘And why not? Youasws are ordering me that I pray one Witr (Salāt) and two Witr (Salāts) in one night’. So heasws said: ‘One of the two is a fulfilment (of an outstanding one)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ’Isma‘il al-Al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The best compensatory prayer for a Salah (prayer) missed is the compensatory prayer during the night for what is missed during the night and what is missed during the day is made during the day.’ I then said, ’So there will be two al-Witr in one night.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, there will not be two al-Witr.’ I then said, ‘Why then do you instruct me to perform two al-Witr in one night?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘One of them is a compensatory prayer for what is missed.’”
